Title: ARDB fix for auto update of .csv files and image hosting.

Messages.Author: drstrange26
Messages.Body:
After having seen the blog by
simidh.blogspot.com/2011/07/brief-review-of-ardb-vs-feldb.html

I was embarrassed as I have replaced ARDB as lead developer.
I am currently working on a new beta for ARDB and having very little access to my building tools so Ive done little to no devleopment. I hope this will change soon.

Please local your ardb.ini ARDB_3_1_1/ardb.ini
Edit that as a text file.
Add the following:
UpdateServer=www.vekn.net
UpdateFile=/images/stories/downloads/vtescsv.zip

This will enable the auto update function of the database to work correctly.
Even as I write this I am working on using the Google Code ARDB site as a place to store the images in .zip format. In the upcoming beta, I will adjust the auto downloader of the images to work correctly. A very small change.
As the original download site no longer exists.

But I need Beta testers!!
Anyone willing to test the updated version please send me a message here (PM of course) with email address and I will send a beta version of 3.1.2Beta.

Please feel free to contact me here or via posting a bug on ARDB.
I cannot fix changes to Mac and am willing to advise anyone willing to try and build and compile on that platform.

Messages.Author: Miasmat
Messages.Body:
A little heads-up about ARDB and saved decks.

code.google.com/p/ardb/issues/detail?id=83

If you reimport the vtescsv.zip and you think something changed, be VERY careful about opening saved decks - they will be changed and AUTOMATICALLY resaved without prompt.

I'd suggest you back up all your saved decks so you don't lose anything just by opening them.

Messages.Author: Miasmat
Messages.Body:
The problem with Pascal's HttB stuff is that the file MUST end in a newline, pretty much, just put a blank line at the end of vtessets.csv.

Actually, same goes for all the .csv files - they have to end with a blank line.

I'd strongly recommend that anyone who wants to edit these .csv files uses a Diff tool (like P4Merge) to compare their changed version with the original.

Oh, and if you ever get any import errors with ARDB, you have to close ARDB, reopen it, import a working vtescsv.zip, close ARDB, reopen it. THEN you can import your (possibly) fixed modified csv.zip. Even though that message pops up about "Rolling back to prevent database corruption" it's a lie. It misses cleaning up something, and you'll have problem on subsequent imports until you reopon ARDB and import successfully.

Messages.Author: thiagotargino
Messages.Body:
Hi! Great job, worked perfectly on Mac.

To edit the ardb.ini on mac, do this:

1) Go to Applications folder on Finder.
2) Right click on ARDB.app and select "Show package contents"
3) Go to the folder Contents/Resources. The ardb.ini is listed there.
4) Edit the file as you should do in Windows and save.
5) Run ARDB again and try to update the database.
6) Smile.

Flip a coin. Thank you.
